Heard Mr.N.L.Rajah, learned Senior Counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioner; Mr.R.Rajesh Vivekananthan, learned Deputy Solicitor General of India appearing on behalf of respondents 1 to 3; and Mr.A.Edwin Prabakar,
learned State Government Pleader for respondents 4 to 6.

2 . The petitioner-trust has filed this petition, pro bono publico, seeking issuance of a writ of mandamus commanding the respondents to take appropriate action for the distribution of nutritious meal to the children eligible under the Puratchi Thalaivar M.G.R.Nutritious Meal Programme in line with the mandates of Sections 5, 6 and 7 read with Schedule II of the National Food Security Act, 2013 on a daily basis.
_ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 3.
When the matter was taken up for hearing, Mr.A.Edwin Prabakar, learned State Government Pleader, drew our attention to the status report filed by the fifth respondent dated 17.4.2024.
The status report speaks for itself.
Paragraph (9) of the status report adumbrates the various instructions issued to the Social Welfare Department during the Covid-19 pandemic.

It is propitious to reproduce paragraph (9) of the status report hereunder:
9.

It is submitted that in addition to the above instructions, the following are the instructions issued to the Social Welfare Department during the Covid- 19 pandemic:-
(i) Letter No.96, Social Welfare & Nutritious Meal Programme (SW4-1) Department dated 14.08.2020 issued by the 4th Respondent
ordered for the continuous provision of dry ration from the month of June 2020 till the reopening of the schools during the lockdown period.

(ii) Detailed Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for distribution of dry rations to the Children so as to ensure the safety and well-being of the __________ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis beneficiaries.

(iii) As per G.O.(MS) No.27, Social Welfare & Nutritious Meal Programme (SW4-1) Department dated 03.09.2020, the Government ordered to provide 10 eggs per month from the month of September 2020 onwards along with dry rations.

sentences.text: Learned State Government Pleader further submitted that the State shall ensure strict implementation of the schemes covering entitlements under Sections 4, 5 and 6 of the National Food Security Act, 2013 and Schedule II thereof, which stipulates the nutritional standards for children in the age group of 6 months to 3 years, age group of 3 to 6 years and pregnant women and lactating mothers, by providing Take Home Rations or nutritious hot cooked meal.
He assured the Court that the implementation of the aforesaid schemes shall not be dispensed with for any reason.
5. Recording the aforesaid submissions made by learned State Government Pleader, the writ petition is disposed of.
If any breach __________ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis is noticed, it is always open to the petitioner to approach the authority concerned.
There shall be no order as to costs.
Consequently, W.M.P.No.14499 of 2021 is closed.
(R.M.D., ACJ.)
